sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme tax deductions
sections.summary: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme gives enhanced tax deductions and allowances for five innovation activities from YA 2024 to YA 2028, with an optional cash payout.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We thank the respondents for their inputs and have taken their feedback on board where feasible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We introduced the Enterprise Innovation Scheme (EIS) to encourage businesses to engage in research and development (R&D), innovation and capability development activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The scheme will be available from year of assessment (YA) 2024 to YA 2028 and grants enhanced tax deductions and allowances for five key activities in the innovation value chain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Under the scheme, eligible businesses can also opt to convert 20% of their total qualifying expenditure on the above activities in each YA into a cash payout of up to $20,000.

sections.label: Foreign sourced disposal gains tax
sections.summary: The new tax treatment applies to foreign sourced disposal gains earned and received in Singapore on or after 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The new tax treatment will apply to foreign sourced disposal gains earned and received in Singapore on or after 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Delivery income tax deduction ratios
sections.summary: Ratios differ by delivery mode; those not opting in can claim actual tax-deductible expenses, effective YA 2024 for income earned in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The ratios will differ depending on the delivery modes, as the workers would use different modes and would incur different levels of expenses, based on IRAS' consultation with the industry and the survey with the workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Those who do not take up this option can continue to claim tax deductions based on the actual amount of tax-deductible expenses incurred in the production of their delivery income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This change found in clause 23 of the Bill will take effect from YA 2024 for income earned in 2023.

sections.label: Fixed deduction for mothers
sections.summary: For children born or adopted from 1 January 2024, mothers get fixed deductions of $8,000, $10,000 or $12,000 instead of a percentage of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For every child born or adopted from 1 January 2024 onwards, the mother will get a fixed deduction of $8,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the second child and $12,000 for any subsequent child and no longer a deduction of 15%, 20% or 25% of her annual income.

sections.label: Mothers earning below $54,000
sections.summary: The question asks how many mothers enjoying the WMCR earn less than $54,000 a year and how many earn more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Taking the latest tax data, how many mothers enjoying the WMCR earn less than $54,000 a year and how many earn more than that amount?

sections.label: R&D tax deduction rate query
sections.summary: The passage asks how the 400% tax deduction rate was decided and whether studies exist on R&D tax deduction changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is especially important in these times of high interest rates, where companies are likely to shelf or postpone their R&D plans, which may require borrowing to fund the significant investment upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, could the Ministry shed light on how it decided on the 400% that the tax deduction will be raised to?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Has there been any studies on how the changes in the tax deduction for R&D over the years had impacted the amount of R&D that is conducted?

sections.label: Rising prices of necessities
sections.summary: The passage lists recent price increases in electricity, gas, transport fares, petrol and Certificate of Entitlement prices, despite a $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I acknowledge the one-off $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living Support Package introduced on 28 September 2023, the recent slew of price spikes of key necessities which could persist well into the future have caused much consternation – with electricity prices up by an average of 3.7% compared to three months ago, gas prices up by 2.3% compared to three months ago, public transport fares set to go up by 7% next year, with another 15.6 percentage points of future fare increases yet to be inflicted on commuters, unleaded 95-octane petrol now close to $3 a litre and, of course, not forgetting Certificate of Entitlement prices which continue to set new record highs with Category A at $105,000 and Category B at $140,889.

sections.label: Higher than expected surpluses
sections.summary: The passage states that FY2022 primary surpluses could be close to $3 billion more than expected, led by record corporate, personal income and GST revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on the latest revenue and expenditure data released on SingStat, it appears that there could be a further close to $3 billion of primary surpluses in FY2022 than what was initially expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is set to be led by corporate income tax, personal income tax and Goods and Services (GST) revenues, which are all set to reach new record highs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But based on just the first five months of the year, operating revenues are already higher by $6.9 billion compared to a year ago.

sections.label: GST hike revenue estimate
sections.summary: The passage states that in Budget 2022 Lawrence Wong said the GST hike will bring about 0.7% of GDP annually, or about $3.5 billion when fully in place in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Budget 2022, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong shared that the GST hike will bring in about 0.7% of gross domestic product (GDP) in revenues annually or about $3.5 billion when the full hike is in place in 2024.

sections.label: Motherhood tax rebate suggestion
sections.summary: The passage asks why a motherhood tax rebate for working mothers earning below a certain income is not given instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If the aim is to benefit lower- to middle-income working mothers, why not just give a motherhood tax rebate to working mothers earning below a certain income?

sections.label: WMCR and grant comparison
sections.summary: The passage states the Government and IRAS can say the WMCR change should not be seen in isolation, and that with the $2,000 grant increase about 97% of mothers would be better or no worse off that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government can say that, look, the change to the WMCR should not be seen in isolation and IRAS can claim that considering both the WMCR change and the one-off $2,000 increase in the Child Development Account First Step Grant in the child's first year of birth, about 97% of mothers would be better off or at least no worse off in that one particular year.

sections.label: Defer GST and review WMCR
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Government will defer raising GST to 9% in 2024 and reconsider WMCR changes, citing Singaporeans' welfare and better-than-expected fiscal position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Considering the welfare of Singaporeans, especially given that the Government's fiscal position is better than expected, collections of corporate income tax, personal income tax and GST are set to hit new record high, and revenue increase has achieved the full year's expected growth in just five months, I hope that the Government will defer its decision to raise GST to 9% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also hope that the Government will reconsider changes to the WMCR to create a family-friendly Singapore.

sections.label: PTIS overseas donation tax deductions
sections.summary: Amendments let family offices with section 13O or 13U awards claim 100% tax deductions for overseas donations through qualifying local intermediaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, the amendments related to PTIS, which allows family offices with approved section 13O or section 13U incentive awards to claim 100% tax deductions for overseas donations made through qualifying local intermediaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The aim is to build on our success in attracting family offices from around the world and to develop Singapore's reputation as a regional philanthropy hub.

sections.label: Local intermediaries overseas donation requirement
sections.summary: Requiring all overseas donations to go through qualifying local intermediaries should spur local charities to build overseas philanthropy capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, the requirement for 100% of overseas donations to be channelled through qualifying local intermediaries should spur local charities to build their capacities and capabilities to meet the requirements for overseas philanthropy.

sections.label: MAS surveys of pilot contributions
sections.summary: MAS said it would conduct regular surveys or analyses, and the speaker hopes new measures are analysed over the five-year pilot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In their reply then, MAS said that they would conduct regular surveys or analyses to obtain a better understanding of these contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope that these new measures, including the development of blended finance structures, climate related investments and charitable contributions, will be analysed over the course of this five-year pilot.

sections.label: IRAS review of FEDR
sections.summary: The speaker asks how often IRAS reviews the FEDR and, if trigger-based, what the triggers are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, in the September Sitting, I had filed a PQ asking if IRAS will consider revising the FEDR – in this specific instance, the 60% FEDR for taxi and private hire drivers in light of higher operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Apart from inflation, there have also been recent corporate actions announced that could have an impact on drivers' earnings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask a clarification of the Minister: how often does IRAS review the FEDR to keep pace with changes in the costs of services?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If it is trigger-based, what are the triggers?

sections.label: Automatic qualification for SEPs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SEPs can be qualified automatically instead of applying for schemes like WIS and others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, can SEPs be qualified automatically rather than having to apply for schemes like the WIS, but also the Majulah Package, the Cost-of-Living Support Package or others?

sections.label: FEDRs for delivery workers
sections.summary: Clause 23 of the Bill proposes introducing FEDRs for self-employed delivery workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 23 of the Bill proposes the introduction of FEDRs for self-employed delivery workers.

sections.label: Income tax refund interest rate peg
sections.summary: Clause 46 amends the interest rate on income tax refunds from the Prime Lending Rate to SORA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 46 of the Bill further amends the interest rate peg charged on the refund of income taxes from the Prime Lending Rate to the Singapore Overnight Rate Average (SORA).

sections.label: CPF interest rate peg reconsideration
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to reconsider the CPF interest rate peg, citing higher yields elsewhere and inflation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even setting aside short-term teaser rates, the yield on the one-year Singapore Government Bills – about as riskless a rate as one can command – currently stands between 3.7% and 3.8%, several multiples higher than the miserly 0.7% for the major local bank average rate, and still more than a full percent higher than the CPF floor of 2.5%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My hon friend and Sengkang colleague, Mr Louis Chua, has repeatedly banged on this drum in the past, and I continue to bang that self-same drum, urging the Government to reconsider the peg for CPF interest rates, especially that which applies to what is paid on accounts held by retirees who cannot enjoy any upward revision in their incomes to account for the higher inflation eating away at the purchasing power of their hard-earned savings.

sections.label: Second quarter GDP growth
sections.summary: The economy grew 0.1% in the second quarter after a 0.4% contraction in the first quarter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the second quarter, we grew by a mere 0.1%, a harrowing brush with a technical recession, given the 0.4% contraction we experienced in the first quarter.

sections.label: Downgraded full-year GDP forecast
sections.summary: The Ministry of Trade and Industry downgraded its full-year GDP forecast to between 0.5% and 1.5%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry downgraded its full-year GDP forecast to a range of between 0.5% and 1.5%, from 0.5% to 2.5%.

sections.label: Headline inflation at 4%
sections.summary: Headline inflation stands at 4%, twice the MAS target.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Headline inflation still clocks in at 4%, twice as high as the MAS target.

sections.label: Majulah Package National Day Rally
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong announced the $7 billion Majulah Package, funded from this term of Government's resources.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, in his National Day Rally this year, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong announced the $7 billion Majulah Package, which he stated would be funded from "resources from this term of Government".

sections.label: Delivery workers tax deduction
sections.summary: New section 14ZH covers delivery service workers and allows self-employed delivery workers automatic tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A new section – 14ZH of the principal Act – covers workers performing delivery services.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 14ZH offers certainty that self-employed delivery workers will now be allowed automatic tax deduction.

sections.label: Innovation tax deductions and payouts
sections.summary: The Bill raises tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure in five innovation areas and allows converting 20% of qualifying expenditure into a cash payout up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many small firm owners shared the same sentiment.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to raise tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure in five areas of innovation activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also allows businesses the option of converting 20% of their total qualifying expenditure per YA into a cash payout of up to $20,000.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and EIS subsidies
sections.summary: For SkillsFuture Singapore approved courses, firms bear only unsubsidised fees, and the EIS could set aside a block budget for upfront innovation project subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For courses approved by SkillsFuture Singapore, firms need only bear the unsubsidised portion of course fees; the training institution offsets the balance from a SkillsFuture Singapore block budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, the EIS could set aside a block budget to provide upfront subsidy for innovation projects of EIS-supported firms.

sections.label: Support for small firms and freelancers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government could explore less cash-taxing innovation arrangements and greater training support for freelancers and SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To lessen the cash burden on small firms, could the Government explore offering firms innovation-supportive arrangements that are less taxing on cash-flow?

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the same vein of enabling small businesses, could the Government consider allocating greater training support for freelancers and SEPs who want to upskill to supply to innovating firms?

sections.label: Non-taxable cash payout option
sections.summary: Offering a non-taxable cash payout option is a practical option for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Offering a non-taxable cash payout option is a practical option for businesses.

sections.label: Scheme extension beyond 2028
sections.summary: The passage asks what indicators MOF will track to decide whether to extend the scheme beyond work year 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Long-term commitment is required for the scheme to be effective and given that the scheme will run out after the work year 2028, what are the indicators that MOF will track while deciding whether to extend it beyond 2028?

sections.label: Overseas donations tax deductions
sections.summary: The scheme allows family offices to claim tax deductions for overseas donations made through qualifying local intermediaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This scheme's global outlook is one of its distinguishing features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We demonstrate our commitment to supporting philanthropic efforts beyond our borders by allowing family offices to claim tax deductions for overseas donations made through qualifying local intermediaries.

sections.label: Transparent eligibility conditions
sections.summary: Eligibility conditions must be transparent and clearly defined so family offices understand the criteria for participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: To ensure that family offices understand the criteria for participation, the eligibility conditions must be transparent and clearly defined.

sections.label: New section 10L foreign asset gains
sections.summary: New section 10L taxes gains from foreign asset sales by entities in a multinational group, deeming them income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The present amendments introduce the new section 10L of the Income Tax Act, which brings to tax gains from the sale of foreign assets by entities that are part of a multinational group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there are exceptions carved out in the new section 10L, the amendment has the broad effect of deeming as "income" in nature, gains which prior to this amendment may have been characterised as capital gains.

sections.label: New section 37AA PTIS
sections.summary: The new section 37AA introduces the PTIS for family offices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next provision I would like to address in the Income Tax Amendment Bill is the new section 37AA, which introduces the PTIS for family offices.

sections.label: Donor prejudice and fund manager conditions
sections.summary: The speaker asks if steps ensure donors are not unfairly prejudiced by conditions subsequent imposed on fund managers, and welcomes the 250% tax deduction extension to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These fund managers may not be entities that the approved donors actually have any control over, and so, I would like to clarify if any steps are being taken to ensure that such donors are not unfairly prejudiced in the event that the authorities decide to unilaterally impose "conditions subsequent" on their fund managers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I acknowledge that the proposed amendments today extend the application of the 250% tax deduction on donations to local IPCs all the way to 2026, which is a very welcome move.

sections.label: Charity sector receipts shares
sections.summary: Arts and heritage charities received 5.8% of annual receipts, while education and social welfare charities took almost two-thirds in FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the 2021 report by the Commissioner of Charities, arts and heritage charities received only 5.8% of all annual receipts in the charities sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In contrast, charities in the education and social welfare sector accounted for almost two-thirds of the total receipts received in FY2020.

sections.label: PTIS funding for local charities
sections.summary: The PTIS can potentially provide a new funding source for local charities, creating diversity in funding sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Particularly in the arts, the PTIS can potentially provide a new source of funding for local charities and, in my view, this can create some much-needed diversity in terms of funding sources.

sections.label: Government help for local charities
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will help ensure local charities and IPCs can access new philanthropic funding from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we certainly cannot force philanthropic organisations to donate their money locally if they do not wish to do so, it is my hope that the Government will help to ensure that local charities and IPCs are well poised to avail themselves of the new sources of philanthropic funding in Singapore which will benefit from this new scheme.

sections.label: Tax on foreign asset gains
sections.summary: New section 10L treats gains received in Singapore from selling foreign assets as income chargeable with tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new section 10L treats gains received in Singapore by an entity from the sale of immovable or movable properties situated outside Singapore – referred to in the section as foreign assets – as income chargeable with tax.

sections.label: Economic substance amendment for companies
sections.summary: The amendment affects companies with entities lacking economic substance in Singapore holding foreign assets; companies showing reasonable economic substance are not taxed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment affects only companies that have entities without economic substance in Singapore but hold foreign assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Companies will not be taxed if they can show "reasonable" economic substance in Singapore.

sections.label: Questions on investment vehicles exclusion
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether certain investment vehicles are excluded from the change and seeks confirmation on foreign tax credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are investment companies, investment funds and SFOs investment vehicles that carry on their businesses in Singapore, through Singapore-based fund managers and Singapore-based SFOs with Singapore-based operations excluded from this proposed change?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would also like to seek confirmation that foreign tax credit will be granted if foreign taxes have been levied on these gains.

sections.label: EIS innovation tax deductions
sections.summary: Budget 2023 introduced the EIS enhancing tax deductions for five activities: R&D, IP registration, IP acquisition and licensing, SkillsFuture training, and polytechnic and ITE innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To nurture and encourage innovation, Budget 2023 introduced the EIS that enhances the tax deductions for five very important activities in the innovation value chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These five activities are: R&D conducted in Singapore; registration of IP, including patents, trademarks and designs; acquisition and licensing of IP rights; training via courses approved by SkillsFuture Singapore; and lastly, innovation carried out with polytechnics and the ITE.

sections.label: Taxation of foreign asset gains
sections.summary: Provisions let SMEs opt for cash conversion, and section 10L taxes gains from foreign asset sales received in Singapore by businesses without economic substance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, there are provisions for SMEs or companies that do not generate sufficient profits to benefit from tax deductions to opt for cash conversion instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These changes have the potential to significantly impact some corporates, fund management companies and family offices operating in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am referring to the introduction of section 10L, the taxation of gains from the sale of foreign assets received in Singapore by businesses without economic substance in our country.

sections.label: Cost-of-living support packages
sections.summary: Three packages totalling over $3.5 billion were rolled out up to February, and another $1.1 billion package was announced last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While this has eased the pressure on headline inflation, inflation rates are still higher than what Singaporeans are used to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, up to February this year, we have rolled out three packages to address cost-of-living concerns totalling more than $3.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And just last week, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced another $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living Support Package to help Singaporeans cope with higher inflation and cost-of-living challenges.

sections.label: EIS qualifying expenditure deductions
sections.summary: The EIS enhances tax deductions of up to 400% of qualifying expenditure on five core activities, including R&D, IP registration and SkillsFuture-approved training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The EIS will enhance the tax deductions of up to 400% of qualifying expenditure on five core activities: qualifying R&D activities, registration of IPs, acquisition and licensing of IP rights, innovation projects carried out by polytechnics, ITEs and qualified partners, and training via courses approved by SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Eligible EIS training courses
sections.summary: The go.gov.sg/eis-training link leads to 12,523 course records, listing topics from AI and machine learning to wine appreciation and 3D jelly art.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Clicking on the link of eligible courses found on go.gov.sg/eis-training leads us to 12,523 course records, listing anything from artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to wine appreciation and 3D jelly art.

sections.label: Lean Six Sigma certification requirement
sections.summary: In the Lean Six Sigma black belt certification, the trainee must show cost savings delivered to his organisation before receiving certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, in the Lean Six Sigma black belt certification where although the course fee is $9,000, the trainee must show that he is able to apply his skills and deliver cost savings to his organisation before he receives the certification.

sections.label: Minimum service years for training deduction
sections.summary: The member asks whether a minimum number of years of employee service could be required before training expenditure qualifies for tax deduction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While I appreciate that it covers individuals deployed under central hiring arrangement or even secondment arrangement, can the Ministry consider having a minimum amount of years that the employee has to serve in the company before his training expenditure can be considered for tax deduction?

sections.label: Partner institutions list excludes universities
sections.summary: The partner list includes polytechnics, ITEs and named partner institutions, and asks why local universities and their centres are excluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, the list of partners includes all the polytechnics, ITEs and partner institutions, such as Aquaculture Innovation Centre, Centre Innovation for Complementary Health Products (Temasek Polytechnic) and Precision Engineering Centre of Innovation (SIMTech).

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Is there a reason why local universities and their associated centres are not included as partner institutions?

sections.label: Cost-of-Living package welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker is encouraged by the new $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living package helping lower- to middle-income families with rising costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In catching up on the news of recent initiatives after coming back, I am encouraged by the new $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living package to help tide lower- to middle-income families cope with rising costs.

sections.label: Donation deduction extended to 2026
sections.summary: Clause 32 extends the 2.5 times deduction for qualifying donations to the non-profit sector through 31 December 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore non-profit sector has benefited from the extremely generous deduction of 2.5 times the amount or value of qualifying donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 32 extends this through to 31 December 2026.

sections.label: Tax incentives for overseas giving
sections.summary: The speaker agrees proposed tax incentives for approved beneficiary organisations will enhance giving beyond Singapore's borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It shows us giving goes beyond the material.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I do agree that giving beyond our borders will be enhanced by the proposed tax incentives for approved beneficiary organisations.

sections.label: Co-creation and Forward Singapore
sections.summary: Co-creation enables top-down and ground-up voices to be considered, and Forward Singapore may require difficult questions and systemic changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Co-creation potentially enables wider buy-in at the early stages, enabling the voices from both top-down and ground-up to be given opportunity for consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Forward Singapore will give us a comprehensive picture of the Singapore that we aspire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Achieving this may require asking difficult questions and to agree to systemic changes where necessary.

sections.label: Value of collaboration
sections.summary: History has shown the place and value of collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: History, however, has shown us the place and value of collaboration.

sections.label: Taxing foreign asset disposal gains
sections.summary: This passage addresses taxing gains from the sale or disposal of foreign assets received in Singapore by businesses without economic substance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, on taxing gains from the sale or disposal of foreign assets that are received in Singapore by businesses without economic substance.

sections.label: EIS discussion area
sections.summary: This passage states that the second area of discussion is regarding the EIS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The second area of discussion is regarding the EIS.

sections.label: Social spending and tax space
sections.summary: This passage notes growing social spending needs, the Government's efforts to enhance the social compact, and the launch of the PTIS and clauses 30 and 31.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Third, Sir, our social spending needs are growing and I am heartened by the Government's efforts to enhance our social compact through growing our tax space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also note the launch of the PTIS and the relevant clauses 30 and 31 in the amendment Bill.

sections.label: Sustainable domestic donations and intermediaries
sections.summary: This passage states domestic donations should be sustainable for funding visibility, and asks how many qualifying local intermediaries there are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Domestic donations should also be done in a sustainable way such that charitable organisations have the funding visibility for a longer-term horizon to grow their missions and reach in serving our community and are encouraged to try new, innovative ways to tackle complex emerging social challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask how many qualifying local intermediaries there are.

sections.label: Discourse on attitudes towards taxation
sections.summary: This passage encourages discourse on attitudes towards taxation, aiming for accessible discourse and clear communication of benefits and trade-offs of tax policy changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we talk about the amendments in this Bill, I would like to take a moment to encourage discourse on attitudes towards taxation while staying away from bogeyman tactics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we renew our social compact, as part of the Forward Singapore efforts, we need to have more conversations to build consensus on questions that are fundamental to how we tax different segments and distribute resources equitably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, aim for greater and more accessible discourse around tax that makes it relevant to the everyday person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, we should aim to clearly communicate the benefits and trade-offs of changes to tax policy, to ensure that Singaporeans better understand how these changes affect our shared future.

sections.label: Cap on additional tax deduction
sections.summary: This passage states the prescribed cap of $400,000 additional tax deduction may serve smaller businesses but be less relevant to larger enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the prescribed cap of $400,000 additional tax deduction may serve its intended purpose for smaller businesses, it may be less relevant to larger enterprises.

sections.label: Cash conversion ratio motivation
sections.summary: The cash conversion ratio of 20% may not be sufficient to motivate them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet, the cash conversion ratio of 20% may not be sufficient to motivate them.

sections.label: Working mothers additional income tax
sections.summary: Working mothers of three children earning $7,000 to $12,000 pay $1,000 or more extra income tax, and those earning $12,000 or more pay $5,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, to cite local finance website Dollars and Sense, working mothers of three children, earning between $7,000 and $12,000, would pay an additional $1,000 or more in income tax than before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Likewise, working mothers earning $12,000 or more will have to pay $5,000 or more in additional income tax.

sections.label: WMCR changed to fixed relief
sections.summary: The amendments change the WMCR from a percentage of earned income to a fixed dollar tax relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments also change the WMCR from a percentage of earned income to a fixed dollar tax relief.

sections.label: Family offices overseas donations deduction
sections.summary: The pilot tax incentive in the Bill gives family offices a 100% tax deduction for overseas donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The pilot tax incentive introduced by the Bill offers family offices a 100% tax deduction for overseas donations.

sections.label: Philanthropic giving and fund-raising rule
sections.summary: The 80:20 fund-raising rule still requires 80% of funds raised for foreign charitable purposes to be applied in Singapore, and the Government is asked to consider other tax measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Philanthropic giving should be encouraged across the whole of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the 80:20 fund-raising rule still requires 80% of funds raised for foreign charitable purposes to be applied towards charitable purposes in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we look to grow Singapore's presence as a regional or even global philanthropic hub, will the Government consider what other tax measures can be used to encourage different forms of giving to local, regional and international causes?

sections.label: Foreign-sourced disposal gains tax treatment
sections.summary: Members spoke on the proposed new tax treatment on foreign-sourced disposal gains, and the Bill does not intend to tax capital gains in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee, Ms Nadia Samdin, Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant and Ms Usha Chandradas spoke on the proposed new tax treatment on foreign-sourced disposal gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is not the intent of the proposed amendments in this Bill to tax capital gains in Singapore.

sections.label: Global Anti-Base Erosion Rules
sections.summary: Pillar 2 Global Anti-Base Erosion Rules seeks to impose a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on large MNEs wherever they operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Pillar 2 Global Anti-Base Erosion Rules seeks to impose a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on large MNEs wherever they operate.

sections.label: Intermediaries submit SEP income information
sections.summary: Intermediaries must submit income information of contracted SEPs, and these SEPs cannot opt out of having it submitted to IRAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Intermediaries included in this initiative will need to submit income information of the SEPs whom they have made contracts with and these SEPs cannot opt out of having their income information submitted to IRAS.

sections.label: Workfare qualification after income submission
sections.summary: If the intermediary had submitted his income information to IRAS, he would have automatically qualified for $2,400 of Workfare in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If the intermediary had submitted his income information to IRAS, he would have automatically qualified for $2,400 of Workfare in 2023.

sections.label: Phased implementation starting commission-paying agencies
sections.summary: IRAS will adopt a phased implementation approach, starting with commission-paying agencies in YA2024, as many already submit income information to IRAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: IRAS will adopt a phased implementation approach, starting with commission-paying agencies in YA2024, as many of these agencies are already submitting income information to IRAS.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: Subsequently, actions such as composition or prosecution, which include penalties of up to $5,000, could be imposed for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Subsequently, actions such as composition or prosecution, which include penalties of up to $5,000, could be imposed for non-compliance.

sections.label: WMCR change for working mothers
sections.summary: The change in WMCR will be effected prospectively and apply only to working mothers with qualifying Singapore Citizen children born or adopted on or after 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The change in WMCR will be effected prospectively and apply only to working mothers with qualifying Singapore Citizen children born or adopted on or after 1 January 2024.

sections.label: FDWLR lapse and concessionary levy
sections.summary: The concessionary levy benefits all families needing care help, including non-taxpayers, so the FDWLR lapses from YA2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This concessionary levy directly benefits all families who need help with caring for their dependants, including those who do not pay income tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Therefore, the FDWLR will be lapsed with effect from YA2025.

sections.label: Government expenditure rise to FY2030
sections.summary: Government expenditure is expected to rise from 18% of GDP to potentially over 20% by FY2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Government expenditure is expected to increase from the current 18% of GDP to potentially over 20% of GDP by FY2030.

sections.label: CDC vouchers increase to $500
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong announced a $1.1 billion package raising CDC vouchers from $300 to $500 for all Singaporean households in January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently announced a $1.1 billion support package, and one of these items would be an increase in the CDC vouchers that all Singaporean households will receive in January next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, from $300 it has increased to $500 – $250 for supermarkets and $250 for heartland shops.

sections.label: Assurance Package enhanced over $10 billion
sections.summary: The Assurance Package was enhanced to over $10 billion with the Cost-of-Living package announced last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Assurance Package was most recently enhanced to now a total amount over $10 billion with the Cost-of-Living package announced by the Deputy Prime Minister last week.

sections.label: PTIS uplifts philanthropic capabilities
sections.summary: PTIS requires overseas donations through qualifying local intermediaries and SFOs to appoint a philanthropy professional, uplifting charity sector capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: By requiring that overseas donations take place through qualifying local intermediaries and requiring that SFOs have to appoint and maintain a philanthropy professional, the PTIS serves to uplift philanthropic capabilities within the charity sector in Singapore.

sections.label: 250% tax deduction for local donations
sections.summary: Qualifying local donations to IPCs and eligible institutions get a 250% tax deduction until 31 December 2026, higher than overseas donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For instance, qualifying local donations made to IPCs and other eligible institutions enjoy a 250% tax deduction until 31 December 2026, which is higher than the tax deduction for overseas donations.

sections.label: Business R&D expenditure growth
sections.summary: Business expenditure on R&D in Singapore rose from $3.8 billion to $6.6 billion between 2010 and 2020, indicating businesses' desire to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have seen a promising increase in business expenditure on R&D over the years, from $3.8 billion to $6.6 billion between 2010 and 2020, which points to businesses' underlying desire to innovate.

sections.label: New tax deduction for innovation
sections.summary: A new tax deduction is introduced for innovation project expenditure, which SMEs more commonly undertake, as many SMEs lack scale for their own R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: While SMEs have shown promising growth in R&D expenditure, we recognise that many SMEs are less likely to have the scale to undertake R&D on their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is why we are introducing a new tax deduction for expenditure incurred on innovation projects, which SMEs more commonly undertake, rather than R&D.

sections.label: Enhanced tax deductions for training courses
sections.summary: The EIS introduces enhanced tax deductions for around 10,000 SkillsFuture Singapore-subsidised courses, recognising training's importance to business innovation capability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We recognise the importance of training workers to support a business' capability to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Hence, the EIS introduces enhanced tax deductions for around 10,000 SkillsFuture Singapore-subsidised courses.

sections.label: Firm co-payment for training
sections.summary: Even with the 400% tax deduction, a firm will need to co-pay for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Even with the 400% tax deduction, a firm will need to co-pay for training.

sections.label: Training cap and scheme monitoring
sections.summary: The $400,000 training expenditure cap mitigates abuse risk, and the Government will monitor EIS take-up, R&D and innovation investments and feedback to review and refine the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The $400,000 training expenditure cap for tax deductions will further mitigate the risk of abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government will monitor the take up of the EIS, businesses' investments in R&D and innovation as well as feedback on the scheme, and these will allow us to continually review the scheme's effectiveness and we will refine it along the way.
